01 · Sales Cube

See the business behind the financial statements

A reconciled analytical foundation for diligence and better business decisions.

A Sales Cube turns transaction-level sales data into a structured, multi-dimensional model. It connects customers, products and services, locations, periods, channels, revenue, and margin in one reconciled view, so you can understand what drives performance and use that insight to make decisions.

The compelling why

Financial results show what happened. A Sales Cube reveals the drivers behind them.

Revenue growth alone does not explain which customers drove it, which products carried the margin, whether retention is improving, or where concentration creates risk. A Sales Cube connects those questions to transaction-level evidence that is reconciled to the books, creating a clearer story of the business and a foundation for ongoing intelligence.

A standalone service. A must-have complement to Quality of Earnings. A Sales Cube can be commissioned independently for business intelligence, transaction readiness, or ongoing monitoring. It is also commonly embedded within a QoE engagement, where financial diligence and commercial analytics support one another.

Sales Cube: commercial drivers

Who drives growth, what customers buy, where margins differ, how durable revenue is, and which operating trends deserve attention.

Quality of Earnings: financial performance

Historical earnings, adjustments, revenue and expense quality, and the financial trends supporting the transaction.

Sell-side: tell the story

Understand the business before a buyer defines it. Give owners, management, and bankers reconciled evidence to explain growth, risks, and opportunities.

Buy-side: test the thesis

Look beyond aggregate results. Evaluate concentration, retention, customer movements, product mix, and margin to inform the investment case.

Management: keep using the insight

Use a Sales Cube independently of a transaction or carry diligence work into ongoing business intelligence, rather than leaving the analysis in a deal folder.

02 · Sales Cube

One reconciled model. Many views.

Every transaction. Every reconciled view.

A Sales Cube is a transaction-level analytical model organized by customer, product or service, location, period, channel, and other dimensions that explain business performance. It is more than a dashboard: it is the reconciled data foundation underneath the analysis.

The questions it answers

Many lenses on the same reconciled data

Revenue

Where is growth coming from?

  • Monthly, annual, and TTM trends
  • Growth by segment and period
  • Price vs. volume, where data supports it

Customers

Who drives the business, and do they stay?

  • Concentration: top 1 / 10 / 20
  • New, existing, lost, returning
  • Retention, churn, and cohorts

Recurring Revenue

How durable is the revenue?

  • Recurring vs. non-recurring split
  • MRR / ARR and revenue bridges
  • Rent roll and contract analyses

Products & Services

What do customers buy?

  • Mix and mix shift over time
  • Top products and service lines
  • Cross-sell penetration

Margin

Where do we make money?

  • Gross margin by customer, product, and location
  • Margin trend and dispersion
  • Requires COGS at the transaction level

Locations & Segments

How do the parts compare?

  • Location, entity, and region performance
  • Salesperson and channel views
  • Platform and add-on combinations

What goes in

Start with the data you have

ERP and QuickBooks exports, Excel and CSV files, PDF reports, SQL backups, CRM and operating systems, and data warehouses or lakehouses such as Snowflake can all contribute to the model. General ledger and financial records provide the reconciliation foundation.

Flexible by design: Sales Cubes come in many shapes and sizes. We tailor the analyses to the business model, available fields, and decisions that matter. Recurring revenue, price/volume, margin, and other specialized analyses are used where appropriate and supportable.

What comes out

Finish with the insights you need

Excel-first, not Excel-only. Deliverables are selected around your business questions, audience, and intended use, from a focused analytical package to interactive reporting and a reusable data foundation.

XLExcel exhibits

Model-ready schedules for PE sponsors, lenders, and bankers. Formatted for the data room and the CIM.

DBInteractive dashboard

Drill into revenue by customer, product, location, and period. Runs as a self-contained file.

RCReconciliation pack

Bridges from source to GL to deliverable, with an exception log and documented judgments.

DTReconciled dataset

The clean Sales Cube data, ready for the buyer's model or for post-close use.

Documentation and executive findings

Data dictionaries, business rules, methodology, KPI definitions, executive findings, and management readouts can accompany the analytical deliverables.

From analysis to ongoing intelligence

Receive a Sales Cube deliverable for a defined need, or extend the foundation through TAS Nexus with managed data, automated reporting, and dashboards for continued monitoring, as scoped to your needs.

03 · Sales Cube

Sales Cube Methodology

Understand · Correct · Prove · Structure · Reveal · Communicate

We do not simply visualize the data received. We inventory it, test it, remediate it, reconcile it to the books, apply documented business rules, and then analyze and communicate the results.

01

Data Management: Understand

Catalog sources and files; assess completeness, accuracy, and consistency; identify missing values, duplicates, and anomalies.

02

Data Remediation: Correct

Clean and standardize records, formats, naming conventions, and data types. Enrich only from trusted, supportable sources and validate the corrected data.

03

Data Reconciliation: Prove

Compare operational detail to the general ledger and financial records. Investigate differences, resolve mismatches, and document adjustments and remaining exceptions.

04

Data Modeling: Structure

Organize transaction-level facts and business dimensions. Apply agreed business rules and build a reusable model that can scale with the business.

05

Data Analysis: Reveal

Identify growth drivers, trends, risks, and opportunities using validated data. Translate findings into decision-relevant business insights.

06

Data Reporting: Communicate

Deliver Excel schedules, dashboards, datasets, summaries, and readouts tailored to stakeholders, with appropriate access and confidentiality controls.

The defining control

Reconciled before relied upon

Source completeness, record counts, control totals, duplicate and missing-value testing, sign validation, period completeness, customer and product mapping, general-ledger tie-outs, and exception logs establish traceability from source records to deliverables.

Reconciliation is the foundation: differences and adjustments remain visible and documented. A polished chart is not a substitute for supportable data.
